answer: A bonded-inlet gate resists sybils: each agent must push its work through one rate-limited inlet whose scarce slot it buys and locks collateral behind, a genuine pearl, not a cheap umber fake. The gate meters real throughput per identity, so clones stuffed behind a single inlet only split its capped bandwidth and choke each other. To give N fakes full standing an attacker must fund N separately-bonded inlets, so cost rises linearly as N times locked capital plus N times recurring bandwidth, never amortized away.
